---
title: "Project roadmap"
---

PRESS combines a reusable inference package with a portfolio documenting its five fitted components, their evaluation and descriptive pressure reports. This page summarizes the completed work and possible research extensions.

## Current state

- **Five fitted components:** [ball-drive risk](vignettes/01_ball_drive_risk/01_ball_drive_risk.ipynb), [pass probability](vignettes/02_pass_probability/02_pass_probability.ipynb), [pass selection](vignettes/03_pass_selection/03_pass_selection.ipynb), [action selection](vignettes/04_action_selection/04_action_selection.ipynb) and [residual risk](vignettes/05_residual_risk/05_residual_risk.ipynb). The package includes the production refits. The active ball-drive solver is the final spline model.
- **Held-out evaluation:** the [benchmark pages](benchmark.qmd) distinguish match-level held-out predictions from production refits, describe fold-specific feature construction and report predictive metrics and calibration. The [composed-risk benchmark](benchmarks/06_composed_risk.qmd) evaluates h and xLoss separately from their component models.
- **Real-match examples and reports:** model examples use observed tracking frames and package plots. The [pressure report](vignettes/07_case_studies/07_case_studies.ipynb) includes pressure escape, drawing pressure and sustained carrying, together with exposure summaries and expected-minus-observed failures per 100 elevated-risk actions. These are descriptive summaries, not player rankings.
- **User-facing API:** the [three-part user guide](usage.qmd) covers preprocessing, segmentation and an end-to-end real-match workflow. The reference is organized into [initialization and classes](api.qmd), [solvers](solvers.qmd), [getters](reference/getters.qmd) and [plots](reference/plots.qmd). Match input tables have explicit contracts, and result exports can be saved and reloaded.
- **Spatial features: accessibility and value:** [BCOS](vignettes/spatial_features/bcos/10_bcos.ipynb) and [xT](vignettes/spatial_features/expected_threat/11.expected_threat.ipynb) have separate definitions, examples and numerical or resolution checks.

- **Research pipeline:** numbered feature, fitting, scoring and production-refit stages live in `pipeline/`. The [pipeline page](pipeline.qmd) gives the dependency order, commands and output layout.

The training pipelines remain a work in progress and will continue to be revised after the initial release. Changes to estimation or validation procedures will be documented and accompanied by updated benchmark results.

## Possible research extensions

**High-risk calibration and component performance.** Investigate the High band of h in greater detail, separating limited-sample uncertainty from possible calibration errors in the passing and carrying branches. Review discrimination and calibration across the five individual tasks and their contribution to composed risk, retaining held-out evaluation and uncertainty estimates. Seek additional tracking-and-event datasets to expand the sample and assess whether the findings persist beyond the current ten matches, checking compatibility of action labels and outcome definitions before comparison or pooling.

**A richer description of accessible space.** Explore directional, radial and spatial summaries of the BCOS field beyond its total area. Their additional value for action selection and residual risk would need held-out evaluation. The current scalar already combines movement and defensive reachability; richer summaries should demonstrate useful information beyond the existing features.

**Pressure lines after a hypothetical turnover.** Evaluate including the original ball carrier when constructing their team's pressure lines for the failed-pass branch of action selection and residual risk. From the recovering team's perspective, that player becomes an opponent who may contribute to the defensive structure. The current features exclude the original carrier from their own team's line construction in both pass-outcome branches; this extension would require recomputing the affected features, refitting and held-out comparison.

**Consistent one-second reference for carrying features.** In action selection and residual risk, teammate and opponent counts ahead of the carrier currently use the carrier's present position, whereas carrying-related xT and pressure-line descriptors use the one-second projection. Evaluate moving the reference line for both counts to that same projected carrier position, retaining current player positions, the strict longitudinal comparison and the exclusion of the carrier. This would align the feature conventions and requires recomputing the affected features, refitting and held-out comparison.

**More data and alternative predictors.** Repeat the tree-model and training-only resampling comparisons on a larger sample, using Stalpaert as a methodological reference [@stalpaert2022]. The existing CatBoost experiment did not establish a resampling benefit. A flexible model could use physical risk together with contextual features, while the present package retains the explicit ball-drive likelihood.

**Unobserved engagement and tactical information.** Body orientation, foot-level control and individual skill are not directly represented. Seek 3D tracking or pose datasets with sufficient detail to study body orientation and player–ball interaction; the availability of suitable public datasets remains to be established. Richer video observations and models of collective defensive interaction could address other parts of this limitation. Larger samples would also permit stronger assessment across teams, competitions and match contexts. Such extensions require new evidence and validation; they are not changes to the current fitted model.
